INTRODUCTIONM
This lesson introduces digital circuits that have the ability to remember the last input, even when the input is removed.
Circuits that remember information are important for the operation of simple calculators and complex computers.
There are many devices used to remember information. In this lesson we will look at one of the simplest, the flip-flop.
Let's begin the lesson on INTRODUCTION TO FLIP-FLOPS......................
LESSON MENU
SEQUENTIAL CIRCUITS
DIGITAL CIRCUITS
DISCUSSION
There are two categories that digital circuits fit into. The difference between the two is in how they produce outputs.
The combinational circuit can produce an output only when an input is applied.
Remove the input condition and the output is stopped.
Stated another way, "Combinational circuits do not remember input conditions". The condition must be present for an output to occur.
The sequential circuit produces an output when an input is applied.
Remove the input condition and the output will remain.
Stated another way, "Sequential circuits remember input conditions. "An input need only be applied momentarily to produce an output.
The sequential circuit uses a feedback signal taken from the output and applies it back to the input.
In this example, the high applied to the input results in a high at the output.
A high feedback signal is taken from the output and applied back to the input.
The purpose of the feedback signal is to allow the circuit to remember the last input signal after the signal is removed.
Even after the input is removed, the output stays high because the high feedback signal creates a loop.
The outputs produced by sequential circuits are described as the output "STATE" of the circuit.
Just as in combinational circuits, the output state is high or low. One output is called Q and the other Q (NOT Q).
When a high is present on Q, the output state is Q.
When a high is present on Q, the output state is Q.
What is the output state of this circuit?
The output state depends on which output results in a high condition. In this circuit, the high is applied to input Q.

What is the output state of this circuit?
The output state depends on which output results in a high condition. In this circuit, the outputs are both low. The output is unknown...

Sequential circuits remain in one STATE until an input places them in the opposite state.
In this simple circuit, the S input is the SET and the R input is the RESET.
When the circuit is in the SET condition the output state is Q.
When the circuit is in the RESET condition the output state is Q.
What is the condition of this circuit?

This circuit is shown in the RESET condition. With a high applied to R the Q output is high.
What is the condition of this circuit?
This circuit is shown in an unknown condition. With two highs applied, Q and Q are in the same state. They must hold opposite states....
TRY AGAIN!
The simple sequential circuit will have a SET and RESET input, Q and Q output, and a feedback signal to remember previous conditions.
This completes the information on SEQUENTIAL CIRCUITS.......
1. The simple sequential circuit has two inputs and two outputs.
2. The inputs are labeled as SET and RESET. SET applies a high to the Q output. RESET applies a high to the Q output.
3. Feedback is used in sequential circuits to allow them to remember input signals after the signals are removed.

DISCUSSION
The flip-flop is a simple sequential circuit that can remember an input condition. It only changes states when a different input condition is applied.
The symbols used for flip-flops vary from boxes to vertical rectangles with two inputs and two outputs.
The flip-flop is a storage device that can remember or forget information. The SET input is used to remember and the RESET is used to forget.
The flip-flop is often called a latch because it is held or fastened like a mechanical latch in one state or the other.
The simplest flip-flop or latch is constructed from a single gate. Feedback is taken from the output and connected to the input.
If highs are applied to inputs A and B the output is a high Q. Feedback is applied to input A to hold the output at Q.
If the inputs are removed the output is still latched in the high Q state.
Only when the input signals produce a low output can the latch change to the Q state.
What is the output state of this flip-flop?
The AND gate Truth Table shows that a high and low input produce a low output.
TRY AGAIN!
This simple flip-flop can only produce a Q output or a Q output. Not both at the same time.
Connecting two gates together allows the flip-flop to produce Q and Q outputs at the same time.
If a high is applied to inputs A, B or both this flip-flop is SET.
A high results on Q and a low results on Q.
If both inputs are low the flip-flop changes state. The Q output goes high and the Q output goes low.
What is the output state of this flip-flop?
The NOR gate Truth Table shows that a high and low input produce a low output. The Q output is low.
TRY AGAIN!
Some flip-flops have an additional input used to gate the Set or Reset input through.
The gate input could be a single pulse. If the Set input is high at the same time the gate pulse is high the flip-flop is Set.
If the Reset input is high at the same time the gate pulse is high the flip-flop is Reset.
The gating input can also be a timing signal produced by a series of square waves.
The flip-flop will change state only when the gating signal and the set or reset signals are high at the same time.
What output state is enabled by this flip-flop?
The gate enables the input condition that is high at the time the gate is high. The output state is a reflection of the input enabled.
TRY AGAIN!
Remember, the flip-flop or latch uses feedback to store the last input condition. It will change only when a different input condition is applied.
This completes the information on THE FLIP-FLOP.TLE........
1. The flip-flop is a simple sequential circuit that can remember an input condition. It only changes states when a different input condition is applied.
2. The symbol used for the flip-flop is a vertical rectangle with two inputs and two outputs.
3. The flip-flop is a storage device that can remember or forget information. The SET input is used to remember and the RESET is used to forget.
4. Some flip-flops have a gate input. The gate input is used to select the SET or RESET condition.
